passages.text: This is the burden against the Desert by the Sea: Like whirlwinds sweeping through the Negev, an invader comes from the desert, from a land of terror.
passages.sermon:
This message is a prophecy against the Desert by the Sea.
A burden is placed upon this land.
A powerful force comes like whirlwinds.
These whirlwinds sweep through the Negev.
An invader comes from the desert.
This invader comes from a land filled with terror.
passages.original: מַשָּׂ֖א מִדְבַּר־ יָ֑ם כְּסוּפ֤וֹת בַּנֶּ֙גֶב֙ לַֽחֲלֹ֔ף מִמִּדְבָּ֣ר בָּ֔א מֵאֶ֖רֶץ נוֹרָאָֽה׃

passages.text: A dire vision is declared to me: “The traitor still betrays, and the destroyer still destroys. Go up, O Elam! Lay siege, O Media! I will put an end to all her groaning.”
passages.sermon:
Isaiah is a prophet.
God gives Isaiah a harsh vision.
The vision is difficult and troubling.
A traitor continues to betray.
A destroyer continues to destroy.
God commands Elam to go up.
God commands Media to lay siege.
God promises to stop all her groaning.
passages.original: חָז֥וּת קָשָׁ֖ה הֻגַּד־ לִ֑י הַבּוֹגֵ֤ד׀ בּוֹגֵד֙ וְהַשּׁוֹדֵ֣ד׀ שׁוֹדֵ֔ד עֲלִ֤י עֵילָם֙ צוּרִ֣י מָדַ֔י כָּל־ אַנְחָתָ֖ה הִשְׁבַּֽתִּי׃

passages.text: Therefore my body is filled with anguish. Pain grips me, like the pains of a woman in labor. I am bewildered to hear, I am dismayed to see.
passages.sermon:
The prophet Isaiah speaks.
He receives a dire vision from God.
His body is filled with anguish.
Pain grips him.
The pain is like the pains of a woman in labor.
He is bewildered when he hears the message.
He is dismayed when he sees the vision.
passages.original: עַל־ כֵּ֗ן מָלְא֤וּ מָתְנַי֙ חַלְחָלָ֔ה צִירִ֣ים אֲחָז֔וּנִי כְּצִירֵ֖י יֽוֹלֵדָ֑ה נַעֲוֵ֣יתִי מִשְּׁמֹ֔עַ נִבְהַ֖לְתִּי מֵרְאֽוֹת׃

passages.text: My heart falters; fear makes me tremble. The twilight of my desire has turned to horror.
passages.sermon:
The prophet Isaiah speaks.
His heart falters.
Fear makes him tremble.
The evening, once his time of longing, now brings him terror.
passages.original: תָּעָ֣ה לְבָבִ֔י פַּלָּצ֖וּת בִּֽעֲתָ֑תְנִי אֵ֚ת נֶ֣שֶׁף חִשְׁקִ֔י שָׂ֥ם לִ֖י לַחֲרָדָֽה׃

passages.text: They prepare a table, they lay out a carpet, they eat, they drink! Rise up, O princes, oil the shields!
passages.sermon:
People prepare a table.
They spread out a carpet.
They eat.
They drink.
Princes, stand up.
Oil the shields.
passages.original: עָרֹ֧ךְ הַשֻּׁלְחָ֛ן צָפֹ֥ה הַצָּפִ֖ית אָכ֣וֹל שָׁתֹ֑ה ק֥וּמוּ הַשָּׂרִ֖ים מִשְׁח֥וּ מָגֵֽן׃פ

passages.text: For this is what the Lord says to me: “Go, post a lookout and have him report what he sees.
passages.sermon:
The Lord spoke to me.
The Lord gave me a command.
He said, “Go.
Set a lookout in place.
The lookout must watch carefully.
The lookout must report everything he sees.”
passages.original: כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר אֵלַ֖י אֲדֹנָ֑י לֵ֚ךְ הַעֲמֵ֣ד הַֽמְצַפֶּ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר יִרְאֶ֖ה יַגִּֽיד׃

passages.text: When he sees chariots with teams of horsemen, riders on donkeys, riders on camels, he must be alert, fully alert.”
passages.sermon:
The Lord speaks to his prophet.
He commands the prophet to post a lookout.
The lookout must watch carefully.
The lookout sees chariots with teams of horsemen.
He sees riders on donkeys.
He sees riders on camels.
The lookout must stay alert.
He must pay close attention.
passages.original: וְרָ֣אָה רֶ֗כֶב צֶ֚מֶד פָּֽרָשִׁ֔ים רֶ֥כֶב חֲמ֖וֹר רֶ֣כֶב גָּמָ֑ל וְהִקְשִׁ֥יב קֶ֖שֶׁב רַב־ קָֽשֶׁב׃

passages.text: Then the lookout shouted: “Day after day, my lord, I stand on the watchtower; night after night I stay at my post.
passages.sermon:
The Lord gave a command to Isaiah.
Isaiah acted as a lookout.
Isaiah stood on the watchtower every day.
Isaiah remained at his post every night.
Isaiah did not leave his duty.
Isaiah called out to his master.
Isaiah said, “My lord, I stand on the watchtower every day.
I stay at my post every night.”
passages.original: וַיִּקְרָ֖א אַרְיֵ֑ה עַל־ מִצְפֶּ֣ה׀ אֲדֹנָ֗י אָנֹכִ֞י עֹמֵ֤ד תָּמִיד֙ יוֹמָ֔ם וְעַל־ מִ֨שְׁמַרְתִּ֔י אָנֹכִ֥י נִצָּ֖ב כָּל־ הַלֵּילֽוֹת׃

passages.text: Look, here come the riders, horsemen in pairs.” And one answered, saying: “Fallen, fallen is Babylon! All the images of her gods lie shattered on the ground!”
passages.sermon:
A watchman stands on the tower.
He sees riders coming.
The riders come in pairs.
They ride horses.
One rider speaks.
He says, “Babylon has fallen.
Babylon has fallen to the ground.
All the images of Babylon’s gods are broken.
The idols lie shattered on the earth.”
passages.original: וְהִנֵּה־ זֶ֥ה בָא֙ רֶ֣כֶב אִ֔ישׁ צֶ֖מֶד פָּֽרָשִׁ֑ים וַיַּ֣עַן וַיֹּ֗אמֶר נָפְלָ֤ה נָֽפְלָה֙ בָּבֶ֔ל וְכָל־ פְּסִילֵ֥י אֱלֹהֶ֖יהָ שִׁבַּ֥ר לָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: O my people, crushed on the threshing floor, I tell you what I have heard from the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel.
passages.sermon:
God is the LORD of Hosts.
God is the God of Israel.
You are my people.
You are crushed on the threshing floor.
I heard a message from God.
I tell you what I heard.
passages.original: מְדֻשָׁתִ֖י וּבֶן־ גָּרְנִ֑י אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁמַ֗עְתִּי מֵאֵ֨ת יְהוָ֧ה צְבָא֛וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הִגַּ֥דְתִּי לָכֶֽם׃ס

passages.text: This is the burden against Dumah: One calls to me from Seir, “Watchman, what is left of the night? Watchman, what is left of the night?”
passages.sermon:
This message is a prophecy against Dumah.
Dumah is a region or people.
Someone calls to me from Seir.
Seir is a place or region.
The person calls out to the watchman.
The person asks, “Watchman, what is left of the night?”
The person repeats, “Watchman, what is left of the night?”
passages.original: מַשָּׂ֖א דּוּמָ֑ה אֵלַי֙ קֹרֵ֣א מִשֵּׂעִ֔יר שֹׁמֵר֙ מַה־ מִלַּ֔יְלָה שֹׁמֵ֖ר מַה־ מִלֵּֽיל׃

passages.text: The watchman replies, “Morning has come, but also the night. If you would inquire, then inquire. Come back yet again.”
passages.sermon:
The watchman answers.
Morning has come.
Night has also come.
If you want to ask, then ask.
Return and come again.
passages.original: אָמַ֣ר שֹׁמֵ֔ר אָתָ֥ה בֹ֖קֶר וְגַם־ לָ֑יְלָה אִם־ תִּבְעָי֥וּן בְּעָ֖יוּ שֻׁ֥בוּ אֵתָֽיוּ׃ס

passages.text: This is the burden against Arabia: In the thickets of Arabia you must lodge, O caravans of Dedanites.
passages.sermon:
This message is a prophecy against Arabia.
Arabia is a desert region.
God speaks about Arabia.
Caravans travel through Arabia.
The Dedanites are traders who travel in caravans.
God tells the Dedanite caravans to stay in the thickets of Arabia.
The Dedanite caravans must spend the night there.
passages.original: מַשָּׂ֖א בַּעְרָ֑ב בַּיַּ֤עַר בַּעְרַב֙ תָּלִ֔ינוּ אֹֽרְח֖וֹת דְּדָנִֽים׃

passages.text: Bring water for the thirsty, O dwellers of Tema; meet the refugees with food.
passages.sermon:
The people of Tema live in the land of Tema.
Thirsty people come to them.
The people of Tema must bring water for the thirsty.
Refugees arrive in their land.
The people of Tema must meet the refugees with food.
passages.original: לִקְרַ֥את צָמֵ֖א הֵתָ֣יוּ מָ֑יִם יֹשְׁבֵי֙ אֶ֣רֶץ תֵּימָ֔א בְּלַחְמ֖וֹ קִדְּמ֥וּ נֹדֵֽד׃

passages.text: For they flee from the sword— the sword that is drawn— from the bow that is bent, and from the stress of battle.
passages.sermon:
The people of Arabia are fleeing.
They run away from swords.
The swords are drawn and ready to strike.
They also flee from bows.
The bows are bent and ready to shoot.
They escape from the heavy stress of battle.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ מִפְּנֵ֥י חֲרָב֖וֹת נָדָ֑דוּ מִפְּנֵ֣י׀ חֶ֣רֶב נְטוּשָׁ֗ה וּמִפְּנֵי֙ קֶ֣שֶׁת דְּרוּכָ֔ה וּמִפְּנֵ֖י כֹּ֥בֶד מִלְחָמָֽה׃ס

passages.text: For this is what the Lord says to me: “Within one year, as a hired worker would count it, all the glory of Kedar will be gone.
passages.sermon:
The Lord spoke to me.
The Lord is the God of Israel.
The Lord said this message.
The Lord said, “In one year, all the glory of Kedar will end.
A hired worker counts a year carefully.
In the same way, this year will be counted.
After this year, Kedar will lose its glory.”
passages.original: כִּי־ כֹ֛ה אָמַ֥ר אֲדֹנָ֖י אֵלָ֑י בְּע֤וֹד שָׁנָה֙ כִּשְׁנֵ֣י שָׂכִ֔יר וְכָלָ֖ה כָּל־ כְּב֥וֹד קֵדָֽר׃

passages.text: The remaining archers, the warriors of Kedar, will be few.” For the LORD, the God of Israel, has spoken.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD has spoken.
Kedar is a tribe known for its warriors and archers.
Few archers from Kedar will remain.
Few warriors from Kedar will be left.
passages.original: וּשְׁאָ֧ר מִסְפַּר־ קֶ֛שֶׁת גִּבּוֹרֵ֥י בְנֵֽי־ קֵדָ֖ר יִמְעָ֑טוּ כִּ֛י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל דִּבֵּֽר׃ס
